company_at_launch: Johnson & Johnson (BLA holder Centocor Ortho Biotech Inc., a J&J subsidiary)
mechanism: Human IgG1 monoclonal antibody binding the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23 (label: human interleukin-12 and -23 antagonist)
route: subcutaneous; single intravenous induction dose for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis
dosing: Psoriasis (2009 label): 45 mg SC (<=100 kg) or 90 mg SC (>100 kg) at weeks 0 and 4, then every 12 weeks. Crohn's disease (2016 label) and ulcerative colitis (2019 label): single weight-based IV induction, then 90 mg SC 8 weeks later and every 8 weeks
first_us_indication: Adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy
other_us_indications: psoriatic arthritis (adults) 2013-09-20; plaque psoriasis adolescents 12-17 years 2017-10-13; plaque psoriasis pediatric patients 6 years and older 2020-07-29; psoriatic arthritis pediatric patients 6 years and older 2022-07-29; Crohn's disease pediatric patients 2 years and older 2026-04-15; ulcerative colitis pediatric patients 2 years and older 2026-08-28
notes: first_quarter_with_us_sales not confirmed: J&J printed no STELARA sales for any 2009 quarter (sales sat in Other pharmaceutical); the earliest printed quarterly US figure is 2010Q1 (56, as a comparative in the Q1 2011 report). FDA approval 2009-09-25 came two days before J&J fiscal Q3 2009 ended (2009-09-27, per the Q3 2009 10-Q), so the first US sales quarter is 2009Q3 or, more likely, 2009Q4; it cannot be confirmed from a printed figure. Sales rows run 2009Q1 (EU approval announced in the Q1 2009 release) to 2014Q3 to cover both possible launch quarters. Dates: original approval letter (BLA 125261); CD = BLA 761044 original approval (letter 761044Orig1s000); UC = 761044 S-003 / 125261 S-152; PsA = 125261 S-103; adolescents = S-138; ages 6+ = S-150; pediatric PsA = S-161; pediatric CD = 761044 S-020 / 125261 S-172; pediatric UC = 761044 S-021 / 125261 S-173. Action dates from Drugs@FDA overview pages for BLA 125261 and 761044; the 2026 pediatric UC letter cites the 2016-09-23 and 2019-10-18 approvals. Mechanism and dosing from the 2009, 2016 (CD) and 2019 (UC) labels on Drugs@FDA. No change in the company recording sales.

company_at_launch: Johnson & Johnson (BLA holder Centocor Ortho Biotech Inc., a J&J subsidiary); Schering-Plough (later Merck) had ex-US distribution rights outside the US, Japan, Taiwan, Indonesia and China/Hong Kong
mechanism: Human monoclonal antibody to tumor necrosis factor (TNF blocker); binds soluble and transmembrane TNF
route: subcutaneous (SIMPONI); intravenous (SIMPONI ARIA, from 2013-07-18, reported in the same J&J line from 2014)
dosing: RA, PsA, AS: 50 mg SC once a month. UC (2013 label): 200 mg SC at week 0, 100 mg at week 2, then 100 mg every 4 weeks. SIMPONI ARIA (2013 label): 2 mg/kg IV at weeks 0 and 4, then every 8 weeks
first_us_indication: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis (adults; RA in combination with methotrexate)
other_us_indications: SIMPONI ARIA (IV) rheumatoid arthritis with methotrexate 2013-07-18; SIMPONI ARIA ankylosing spondylitis and psoriatic arthritis 2017-10-20; SIMPONI ARIA polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis and psoriatic arthritis in patients 2 years and older 2020-09-29; SIMPONI ulcerative colitis pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg 2025-10-07
notes: first_quarter_with_us_sales not confirmed: J&J printed no SIMPONI sales for any 2009 quarter; the earliest printed quarterly US figure is 2010Q1 (39, as a comparative in the Q1 2011 report). FDA approval 2009-04-24 fell in J&J fiscal Q2 2009 (ended 2009-06-28), so 2009Q2 is the earliest possible US quarter; the Q2 2009 10-Q (filed 2009-08-04) says the J&J subsidiary "also plans to distribute SIMPONI" in the US. Sales rows run 2009Q2 to 2014Q2. Distribution change: under the J&J-Merck settlement of 2011-04-15, J&J began recording SIMPONI (and REMICADE) sales in Canada, Central and South America, the Middle East, Africa and Asia Pacific from 2011-07-01; Merck kept Europe, Russia and Turkey (contribution income split 50/50 from 2011-07-01 to 2024-10-01). Mitsubishi Tanabe holds licensed distribution rights in Japan, Indonesia and Taiwan. J&J said its 2010 SIMPONI sales of $226 million included sales to distribution partner Merck. Merck's own SIMPONI sales in its territories are not in J&J's figures. No change in the company reporting the J&J line. UC = BLA 125289 S-077/S-078/S-079 (letter); SIMPONI ARIA = BLA 125433 (letters for ORIG, S-020/S-021, S-030/S-031); pediatric UC = 125289 S-157. Action dates from Drugs@FDA overview pages.

company_at_launch: Johnson & Johnson (BLA holder Janssen Biotech, Inc.)
mechanism: Human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the p19 subunit of IL-23 (label: interleukin-23 blocker)
route: subcutaneous; intravenous induction option for ulcerative colitis (2024) and Crohn's disease (2025)
dosing: Psoriasis and PsA: 100 mg SC at week 0, week 4, then every 8 weeks. UC (2024 label): 200 mg IV at weeks 0, 4 and 8, then 100 mg SC every 8 weeks from week 16 or 200 mg SC every 4 weeks from week 12. CD (2025 label): same maintenance; induction 200 mg IV or 400 mg SC at weeks 0, 4 and 8
first_us_indication: Adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy
other_us_indications: psoriatic arthritis (adults) 2020-07-13; subcutaneous induction regimen for ulcerative colitis 2025-09-19; plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis in pediatric patients 6 years and older weighing at least 40 kg 2025-09-26
notes: 2017Q3 rests on a derived figure: full-year 2017 US 62 minus Q4 2017 US 46 = 16 (both printed in the Q4 2018 report); J&J printed no TREMFYA line until that report (2019-01-22). Approval 2017-07-13 fell in J&J fiscal Q3 2017 (2017-07-03 to 2017-10-01). The approval source is the Drugs@FDA overview for BLA 761061 (the original letter's first pages are scanned images); the 2025 pediatric letter also cites the 2017-07-13 and 2020-07-13 approvals. UC = S-021, CD = S-024, SC UC induction = S-026, pediatric = S-028/S-029 (letters read). Mechanism and dosing from the 2017, 2024 and 2025 labels. No change in the company recording sales.
